name: Hudson
blurb: Long, slow horizontal swells that drift like the river on a calm day. Reads beautifully under grazing light in lobbies and long corridors.

name: Ridgeline
blurb: Stepped topographic terraces inspired by the Shawangunk and Catskill ridges. Each contour is a flat pocket, so it machines quickly and crisply.

name: Ripple
blurb: Concentric rings spreading from an off-center point, like a stone dropped in still water. Great as a single feature wall.

name: Dune
blurb: Asymmetric diagonal ridges with a soft windward slope and a sharper lee edge, like wind-shaped sand.

name: Tide
blurb: Two wave fields crossing at a shallow angle, creating a soft interference pattern like overlapping wakes.

name: Colonnade
blurb: Classic concave vertical flutes on a 1-1/2" spacing. Timeless on reception desks, columns, bar fronts and feature walls.

name: Reed
blurb: Fine convex reeding on a 3/4" pitch. Adds rich texture to cabinet-style fronts, doors, island panels and headboards.

name: Fade
blurb: Flutes that grow from nothing at the top to full depth at the bottom, a subtle gradient that makes a wall feel taller.

name: Undulate
blurb: Vertical flutes whose depth swells and relaxes in a slow wave across the panel. Flutes and waves in one.

name: Stopped Flute
blurb: Traditional stopped fluting with rounded ends, as on classical pilasters. Perfect for columns, door casings and mantels.

name: Shiplap
blurb: Clean horizontal V-grooves that give the look of shiplap or nickel-gap boards in a single flat, stable panel.

name: Board & Batten
blurb: Raised battens over flat boards, carved from one sheet so there are no seams to open up. Farmhouse to modern.

name: Brick
blurb: Running-bond brick with rounded, slightly irregular faces. Lightweight faux brick for accent walls and fireplaces.

name: Wainscot
blurb: Raised-panel wainscot with beveled fields, carved from one sheet for paneled dining rooms, stair walls and cabinetry ends.

name: Coffer Grid
blurb: A crisp grid of square-bottom grooves. Simple, architectural, and easy to align across full walls or ceilings.

name: Adze
blurb: Staggered scoop marks like a hand-hewn beam, cut with a ball-nose tool for a hand-tooled look at production speed.

name: Chisel
blurb: Random-length vertical gouge strokes with tapered ends. Organic, warm and different on every panel.

name: Birch Bark
blurb: An irregular vertical texture with the stretched, layered feel of bark. Hides fingerprints and wear in busy spaces.

name: Hammered
blurb: Overlapping shallow dimples on a hex grid, like hand-hammered metal, cut in wood or MDF. Stunning in matte black.

name: Pyramid
blurb: A grid of crisp four-sided pyramids cut with a V-bit. Bold shadows that change all day as the light moves.

name: Facet
blurb: Elongated diamond facets, like a cut gemstone stretched tall. Sharp, architectural and easy to scale up or down.

name: Hex Dome
blurb: Softly domed hexagon tiles with a crisp V-groove between each one. Warm and tactile, like a honeycomb.

name: Chevron
blurb: Nested V-groove chevrons that point the eye upward. A strong graphic statement for bars, restaurants and retail.

name: Basket Weave
blurb: Alternating squares of horizontal and vertical ribs, like a woven basket. Great for headboards and accent walls.

name: Scale
blurb: Overlapping scalloped scales, each gently sloped, like shingles or a fish's skin. Beautiful on curved or column surfaces.

name: Sunburst
blurb: Rays fanning out from a low center point, cut entirely with a V-bit. Mid-century energy for entries and headboards.

name: Herringbone
blurb: The classic herringbone floor pattern, V-grooved into a single panel. Looks like dozens of pieces, installs like one.

name: Waffle
blurb: Soft pillowed squares separated by rounded channels, like a waffle or tufted upholstery. Warm and tactile.

name: Fin Wall
blurb: Parallel plywood fins whose outer edge follows a flowing curve. Built from stacked, CNC-profiled sheets, with no two fins alike.
tooling: Profile-cut plywood fins, assembled on a backer

name: Pixel
blurb: A field of square blocks stepped to five depths, driven by a smooth gradient, like a digital landscape. Flat pockets only, so it's fast to cut.

name: Contour Stack
blurb: Stacked plywood layers, each profiled to a slice of a 3D form, so the exposed ply edges draw natural contour lines.

name: Flex Kerf
blurb: Staggered through-slits (a "living hinge") let a flat sheet of plywood bend smoothly around columns, curved walls and reception desks.

name: Tambour
blurb: Solid slats cut almost through, leaving a thin flexible skin (or mounted on fabric), so the panel wraps curves like a roll-top desk.
tooling: Kerf-cut slats or slats on fabric backer

name: Flex Lattice
blurb: A zig-zag lattice screen cut from thin stock that flexes into curves. Popular for curved partitions, pendant shades and ceilings.

name: Flex Wave
blurb: Wavy S-shaped kerf slits that bend in two directions, ideal for curved bar fronts, columns and backlit features.

name: Linear Slot
blurb: Through-cut vertical slots backed with black acoustic felt. Absorbs sound while giving a clean, linear look.

name: Morse
blurb: Slots of varying lengths set in rhythmic columns, like code, cut through and backed with felt for sound control.

name: Perf Grid
blurb: A precise grid of drilled holes with an acoustic backer. Quiet, minimal and highly effective in offices and restaurants.

name: Slat Acoustic
blurb: The classic acoustic slat wall: wood slats on black acoustic felt. Warm, modern and very effective at taming echo.
tooling: Ripped / CNC-cut slats on PET felt backer

name: Groove & Perf
blurb: Fine horizontal grooves with hidden holes behind, the look of commercial acoustic panels used in auditoriums and boardrooms.
tooling: 1/8" end mill grooves + drilled back holes

name: Skyline Diffuser
blurb: A 2D sound diffuser: a grid of blocks at varying depths that scatters sound evenly. A favorite in studios, theaters and listening rooms.

name: Wave Slat
blurb: Acoustic slats whose faces are carved to a flowing wave, so the whole wall moves while still absorbing sound.
tooling: Slats 3D-carved on the face, on felt backer

name: Quatrefoil
blurb: A classic interlocking four-lobed pattern cut through. Works as room dividers, radiator covers and window screens.

name: Cellular
blurb: Organic Voronoi cells with rounded openings, like leaf veins or dried earth. Striking backlit or against a light wall.

name: Honeycomb
blurb: Clean hexagonal openings with an even web. Strong, lightweight and easy to scale for ceilings and partitions.

name: Halftone
blurb: Circles that grow and shrink across the panel to create a gradient, like a printed photo. Can be customized to any image or logo.
tooling: Drilled + 1/4" bit circle pockets, through cut

name: Kasbah
blurb: Eight-point stars and crosses inspired by traditional geometric tile. Rich in pattern yet simple to cut.

name: Birch Stand
blurb: Vertical slats of random widths, like a stand of young trees. A soft, natural divider that still lets light through.

name: Greek Key
blurb: The timeless meander border, repeated as an all-over screen. Classic, orderly and endlessly adaptable.

name: Petal
blurb: Pointed ogee (petal) openings in a staggered repeat. Elegant for room dividers, cabinet inserts and backlit walls.

name: Prism
blurb: Triangular openings in a clean geometric grid. Modern, graphic and strong, great for facades and fences in HDPE or aluminum.

name: Canopy
blurb: Scattered leaf-shaped openings that cast dappled light like a tree canopy. Beautiful as a screen, gate insert or ceiling feature.

name: Ice Ray
blurb: A traditional Chinese "cracked ice" lattice of irregular straight-sided openings. Every section is unique.

name: Rings
blurb: Overlapping circles form a flowing chain-link pattern of petals and rings. Soft geometry that suits homes and hospitality.
